The Helan Mountains, sometimes called a "mountain island in the sky," form a barrier between the semi-arid Ordos Plateau and the Yellow River Valley on one side and the dry deserts of the Alxa Plateau to the west on the other. Like the rugged ranges of western North America's Great Basin, the Helan Range holds dense conifer forests and may support unique endemic communities of plants and animals. The ecoregion has received little scientific attention, yet it is home to several rare species, among them blue sheep, blue-eared pheasants, and the endemic Helan pika. Commercial logging remains a serious threat, and the habitat destruction it causes puts the region's high biological diversity at risk.

# Conservation of Nose-Touch Avoidance Across *C. elegans* and Relatives

Nose touch avoidance behavior is largely conserved among five of the six species tested (Figure 5A). In *C. tripartitum*, animals showed an overall avoidance rate of less than 10% after the first few positive trials, which suggests this species adapts to the nose-touch stimulus faster than *C. elegans* and the others (Figure 5A). During the first three trials, however, *C. tripartitum* responded at levels quantitatively similar to *C. elegans* (Figure S2 in Additional file 2).

Ablating the ASH neurons in five nose-touch responsive species abolished nose-touch avoidance (Figure 5A). Four of the five species still responded in 20–30% of trials (Figure 5A). *Caenorhabditis* sp. 3 was the exception: its ASH-ablated animals completely lost the ability to respond to nose touch (Figure 5A).

Ablation of the AWC neuron, by contrast, had no effect on the nose-touch response in any of the species (Figure S3 in Additional file 2).

In Fig. 15 the alitrunk is conspicuously swollen and sits much higher than the propodeal dorsum. The propodeum bears a pair of strong spines, straight to slightly upcurved. There is no metanotal groove, and the metapleural lobes are triangular and conspicuous. In profile the petiole has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node whose dorsum slopes down posteriorly, giving a short posterior face. On the postpetiole the anterior and dorsal surfaces form a single convexity, and the posterior face is truncated. In dorsal view the nodes of both petiole and postpetiole are broader than long.

The dorsum of the head is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye-level. The rugae are irregular and meander slightly, and a few anastomoses are usually present. The scrobal area is largely smooth, though it usually carries 1–2 fine rugulae crossing its width just behind the antennal fossa. The sides of the head behind the eyes are finely reticulate-rugose, and this sculpture runs around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. The spaces between the rugae are unsculptured, or at most show the faintest superficial traces.

The dorsal alitrunk is everywhere finely but strongly reticulate-rugose, with broad, shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose, while the postpetiole ranges from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured. All dorsal surfaces of the head and body are densely clothed with fine, acute hairs. The color ranges from dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

UPO-06: PrhI Gene Synthesis
UPO-06 carries the coding sequence for prhI from *Ralstonia solanacearum*. PrhI is an ECF sigma factor needed for transcription driven by the Prh signal transduction system. PrhR activates the gene, which then directs sigma factor expression through activation of the PprhJ promoter. The sequence has been optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

UPO-11: PprhJ Promoter Synthesis
UPO-11 provides the PprhJ promoter region. This promoter responds to plant cell contact through signal transduction mediated by PrhA and PrhR, and it is activated by the ECF sigma factor PrhI. The sequence has been optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

Subject: Key findings on foxl2 expression patterns in trout

Dear Customer,

Here is a summary of our findings on foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both foxl2 transcripts were expressed very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a expression was highly restricted in the male, while the diverged paralog foxl2b was present in most adult extragonadal tissues examined (see Additional file 2).

In contrast, foxl2b expression was highly restricted in adult female tissues, essentially confined to the skin, gill, and ovary. foxl2b expression in the testis was very strong, which fits well with previous findings showing foxl2b presence alongside the absence of foxl2a in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Taken together, these results suggest that foxl2b may act as a critical regulator of male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), particularly later in development.

Thank you for your interest in our research.

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation based on the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975). From this we obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Using only the linear dispersion relation for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), known as the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). The leading-order solution shows that the modified curvature terms of the MMSE have significant effects, while the slope square terms stay negligible, as expected under the mild-slope assumption. We therefore kept all the modified curvature terms that are neglected in the MSE, which gave us a uniform model.

We built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM) to predict wave scattering by a varying bottom. In general, the uniform model can predict the main features of waves over different sea beds, such as sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, the uniform model agrees more closely with experimental data than other established models. For man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model agree more closely with experimental data than the results of Kirby (1986).

A key result of the FEM model is its application to wave transformation over arbitrarily-varying bathymetry.

However, Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) cannot back carbon neutrality claims for electrical use beyond a claimant's metered consumption, since most RECs come from projects that were financially viable without their sale. [10] Consequently, they lack the essential attribute of additionality. Additionality examines the counterfactual: what would have happened under the status quo had the REC not been purchased or contracted. While many additionality testing frameworks exist, the core question stays the same: did the project's financial survival depend on REC revenues? Without verified proof of additionality, RECs cannot be treated as genuine emissions offsets.

The myth of the Phaedrus is described with greater intensity than anything that came before it, though it belongs to a different order. It deals with a former existence rather than a future one, and shows a deep conflict between reason, supported by passion or righteous indignation, and the animal instincts within us. In that earlier life, the human soul traveled in the company of some god and saw truth in the form of the universal before birth, and our present existence is the outcome of a struggle that took place then. This world is a relative thing, often projected into a future, much as we wonder where men were before their birth or what awaits them after death. The question "Where were men before birth?" feels unfamiliar and unnatural to us, yet it carries as much force and reach as the other. In the Phaedrus, the "spiritual combat" of this life is only a figure of speech, and the majesty and power of the whole passage, especially the proem beginning "The mind through all her being is immortal," can only be rendered poorly in another language.

Subject: A Note on the Enduring Legacy of Buraq

Dear Friend,

The world once existed as a blend of reality and myth, with a clear distinction between the two emerging only with modern comparative biology. Yet science has not erased the liminal zone where a figure like Buraq resides. We need such transitional objects to connect seemingly divergent realms of empirical knowledge and spiritual experience.

Her presence in contemporary culture serves as a bridge between rationalist taxonomies and the vestigial power of myth. This idea finds its most forceful expression in the Islamic transport industry, where Buraq, a figure combining piety and speed, recurs as a patron saint. She gives her name to airlines from Libya to Indonesia, bus companies, freight ships, motorcycle taxis, a space camp, an engineering college, and even Pakistan's first drone.

The fluidity of Buraq as an aesthetic and linguistic object explains her pliability in commercial use: she presides over wings and wheels, and is also used to sell plastic and PVC, heavy metal, and heavy-duty diesel (BURAQ LUBRICANTS), Indian food, and surgical instruments.

MapleStory Monsters: A Survival Guide to the Underworld

Welcome to the wild world of MapleStory. There are thousands of monsters roaming around, so here is a quick breakdown of where they live and how to survive.

The weak monsters are the most common foes, and they are found by towns. You will see them wandering aimlessly, even if you bump into them. Don't worry, just take the damage they deal.

The dangerous ones are the most lethal monsters, and they live deep in dungeons.

The aggro mechanic is important. Monsters usually roam aimlessly, even if you bump into them. But if you attack an enemy or cast a debuff on it, you will "aggro" it. That means you get its attention, and it will try to attack you back.

The behavioral pattern: most enemies attack by trying to run into you over and over again. Against these persistent attackers, the best strategy is to attack them repeatedly. Your attacks usually have enough knockback to keep them in place. Sometimes you will need to jump over them to dodge their attacks entirely. These are your dodge tactics.

For the full details, check out the complete list of monsters at MapleStory/Monsters/Complete list.

Remember: aggro is a two-way street. Stay safe and keep attacking.

Cell motility matters for more than movement itself. It is central to embryonic development and to many physiological and pathophysiological processes. When its regulation fails, the results are serious, ranging from developmental defects to metastatic cancers.

My research focuses on the basic mechanisms that control how cells move and change shape. Directing cell migration requires constant remodeling of the cytoskeleton, which responds to a variety of extracellular signals, both diffusible and surface-bound.

The question that drives us is this: how do cells convert environmental signals into the precise mechanical forces needed to carry out directed movement? Understanding how molecular cues become physical force is what makes cell migration fully explicable.

The ecoregion covers the moist deciduous forests around the montane rainforests in the northern part of the Western Ghats, in Maharashtra and Karnataka in western India. The region comes from Gondwana. During the Cretaceous period, the Deccan Plate broke away from Gondwanaland, drifted north, and later joined the northern Eurasian continent. Geological uplift then formed the Western Ghats Mountains, which caught the southwestern monsoon rains and produced a moisture gradient, from wet on the windward side to drier habitats on the leeward side. Annual rainfall is 1,500 to 2,000 millimeters, with a dry season lasting 4 to 5 months. The mean annual temperature is between 24 and 27°C, though inland maximum temperatures can exceed 40°C.

We want to share some important information about early hearing development. Humans typically develop spoken language within the first few years of life. Hearing impairment can prevent the ability to speak and also hinder the ability to understand spoken language.

By the time it becomes apparent that a severely hearing-impaired (deaf) child has a hearing deficit, communication problems may have already caused issues within the family and hindered social skills. If the child is part of a Deaf community where sign language is used instead of spoken language, these challenges can be reduced (please see our article on Deaf Culture).

In many developed countries, hearing evaluations happen during the newborn period to prevent the inadvertent isolation of a deaf child within a hearing family. Sign language is a full means of communication, but literacy ultimately depends on the ability to understand speech. In most written language, the sound of the word is coded in symbols.

A person who hears well enough to learn to speak and read will keep the ability to read even if their hearing later becomes too impaired to hear voices. A person who never heard well enough to learn to speak is rarely able to read proficiently (see [4]). Most evidence suggests that early identification of hearing impairment is key to ensuring a child with very insensitive hearing learns spoken language effectively. Listening also plays an important role in learning a second language.

We hope this information helps you understand the importance of early intervention. If you have any further questions, please reach out.

Warm regards,

The large, soft arm-chairs, the full draperies, the eider-down cushions, and all the other refinements that we alone understood in the whole European family, led only to the imprisonment of those who owned them. If you had the misfortune to live in a spacious hotel set back from the street, within a court, to escape the noise and smells, you had your throat cut. That way of treating elegant manners put them out of fashion. Transduction is the process by which physical and chemical signals are converted into neural impulses. In the nervous system, transduction is the basic process of translating stimuli into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, physical or chemical inputs are transformed by specialized sensory receptors into electrical impulses that travel to the brain.

The visual system is a good example. In the retina, rod and cone cells connect the physical environment to neural communication. When light strikes these photoreceptors, it causes a conformational change in the protein rhodopsin. This molecular shift starts a cascade of events that changes the electrochemical gradient of the photoreceptor. The reduction in this gradient leads to a decrease in the electrical signals sent to the brain. So more light hitting the photoreceptor results in fewer electrical impulses, which is how the brain decodes the visual world.

Subject: Tips for Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), often just called the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is made up of many former industrial cities, including Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

Around five million people live here, which makes the region much larger than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. There are plenty of motorways, but hitchhiking can be hard because of the complicated network of minor roads. The main motorways are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you plan to hitch here, stay on these primary motorways. The smaller roads are very difficult to work with since hardly any transit traffic uses them. Germany is generally a pleasant country for hitchhiking, but the Ruhr Area is by far its most unpleasant part in this respect. Hitching inside the Ruhr is comparable to hitching in a big city like Istanbul: the cities are independent, but to a traveler they all feel like districts of one huge city.

We hope this helps you plan your trip safely and enjoyably.

Best regards,

Subject: Study Results: Lung Tissue Volume and Aeration Analysis

Dear Customer,

Below are the main findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

Total lung tissue volume was calculated as: volume of lung tissue = number of voxels × volume of the voxel, provided the compartment considered has a CT number above zero.

The change in functional residual capacity from PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) was computed as the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between the PEEP and ZEEP states. Alveolar derecruitment was defined as the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between these same conditions.

We also computed the changes in gas volume from PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated lung regions, defined by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

As described in reference [21], the distribution of lost lung aeration for each patient (lung morphology) was classified as diffuse, patchy, or lobar based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.

Happy to discuss these results further.

Mobile Gaming: The Next Evolution of Co-Creation

Mobile internet expands the immersive potential of storytelling through electronic games that run on portable, location-aware interfaces. This is the latest step in a decades-long evolution of electronic games that try to make the player a co-author alongside the original designers, rather than just an avatar in a gameworld.

Location-aware interfaces let players pull places from the physical world into their gameworld, and the reverse, something no earlier interactive media could do. Beyond giving players a role in worldmaking, mobile games drop linear narratives in favor of cooperative storytelling built on the player's experience of place.

The "author-player" worldmaking idea has existed for some time, and mobile games push the process past the limits of traditional video games. By extending worldmaking beyond the screen and into the physical world, location-aware interfaces use the player's sensory experience of real places as a storytelling tool.

In our essay, we theorize the unique storytelling potential of mobile games and describe our experience trying to put that potential into practice through the design and implementation of our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.
